chain_trace.break_detail: Break is at the contract→claim grounding link, not at doc/script/log. The constraint's assertion text does not ground the claimed phenomenon: (a) it makes no promise about error diagnostics or query-parameter handling, and (b) the probed parameter is undocumented for this endpoint (registry backfill artifact contradicted by the vendor's own v1.18.x OpenAPI and the live doc). The doc link is consistent for what the assertion actually says; the script faithfully executed its (mis-premised) oracle; the log faithfully reflects the raw HTTP behavior. The 400/empty-body itself is real behavior but originates in the HTTP framework layer, not in any qdrant handler (see source_grounding).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /aliases → actix router → get_aliases(dispatcher, auth) → do_list_aliases(toc, auth) (src/common/collections.rs:190-196) → toc.list_aliases → CollectionsAliasesResponse{aliases}. No Query extractor anywhere on this path, so the collection_name query parameter never reaches any validator or handler; actix-web's extractor model silently ignores unknown query keys on handlers without Query<T> — this explains all ten 200 probes. The observed bare 400/empty body cannot originate from qdrant code: no application path reads the parameter, and every application-level rejection in this deployment carries a JSON diagnostic (validator error handler at src/actix/mod.rs:227-254 renders 'Validation error in path parameters: [...]'; StorageError responses render as {"status":{"error":...}} — both observed live in the 422 and 409 comparison lines). The 400 is emitted pre-router by the HTTP/1.1 protocol layer when the ~100KB request line (query string) overflows the actix-http h1 decode buffer, responding with a bare 400 and content-length 0. Supporting correlation: 1MB via body face → 200; short query values (incl. %00, lone-surrogate) → 200; only request-line-length overload → 400. actix-http sources are not locally available (cargo registry cache contains no actix crates), so the exact internal constant could not be quoted from source — the framework-origin conclusion rests on the qdrant-side structural evidence above. Verification outcome reasoning: for the probed face (query param of GET /aliases) the source contains no validation and no handling at all (validation_absent — because the parameter is not part of the endpoint); for the documented faces, validation IS present (CollectionPath 1..=255 + charset at the path face, JsonConfig limit at the body face). No by_design_in_source marking: no comment/docstring/maintainer citation in the tree declares intent about empty-body 400s or about ignoring unknown query params — the silent-ignore behavior is unannotated framework default, which per the rules cannot be marked by_design.
